name.text: Using Geometric Formulas to Calculate Definite Integrals (Polygons)

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the integral to find the area under the curve: \(\displaystyle \int_{@lower@}^{@upper@} {@func1@} dx\)

Hint: You will have to sketch the function.


\( A = \)[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The graph of the function \(y= {@func1@}\) over the interval \(\left( 0,{@upper@}\right)\) is shown below.


[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [0, 10, 8, -2], keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation: true }); // Define the function y = mx + c function f(x) { var m = {#grad#}; var c = {#intercept#}; return m * x + c; } // Create the curve for y = mx + c var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [f, -1, 7]); // Create the point var point1 = board.create('point', [0, 0], { name: ''} ); var point2 = board.create('point', [{#upper#},0], { name: '' }); var point3 = board.create('point', [{#upper#}, {#height#}], { name: 'y={#func1#}' }); // Create the polygon using points p1, p2, and p3 var polygon = board.create('polygon', [point1, point2, point3], { fillColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.3)' }); [[/jsxgraph]]

To calculate the area under curve we'll use the formula \(\displaystyle A= \frac{1}{2}b \times h\)

\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}\times {@base@} \times {@height@}= {@ta@}\)
